text:
Good morning, and happy Election Day. It's a cloudy, mild start, 53 right now, and we stay gray through the day. A few light showers drift in after lunch, mostly between 1 and 5, and they won't amount to much, just a few hundredths of an inch. The high is near 61. If you're heading to the polls, a light jacket will do, and the morning is the driest stretch. Tonight is mostly cloudy and mild, with a low around 53 and maybe a leftover sprinkle before 9.

Wednesday is the standout. Sunshine and a steady south breeze push us to around 71, with a shot at a few daily records. The models range from the upper 60s to low 70s, so I'd lean toward the warm side. Enjoy it, because it won't last.

Rain arrives early Thursday, likely by daybreak, though it looks lighter than it did a day ago, probably under a quarter inch. Highs stay in the 60s. Then the weekend turns noticeably cooler, with showers possible Saturday. Take Wednesday afternoon for your outdoor errands.

week.blurb: Cloudy and mild with a high near 61, and a few light showers possible after mid-morning, nothing more than a sprinkle.
Mostly sunny and warm with a high near 71, easily the nicest day of the week, and it stays dry.
Showers likely from the morning on with a high near 66, and the European model runs wetter, so carry the umbrella.
Cloudy and a touch cooler with a high near 63, and showers possible from the morning on into the evening.
Looks like a cloudy, cooler Saturday with a high near 56 and a decent chance of showers at times.
Trending drier with some sun breaking through, a high near 53, and just a stray shower possible before early afternoon.
If the pattern holds, a chilly Monday near 51 with a little sun and a chance of showers returning.

AFD DISCUSSION (the forecaster's full reasoning, same regional caveat; their temps are area-wide ranges):
KEY MESSAGE 1: Breezes will remain southerly today and tomorrow, but will be increasing. Gusts 15 to 25 mph can be expected today, especially in the northern Champlain Valley and St. Lawrence Valley. Wednesday will see a surge of warm air advection as southerly flow deepens and the pressure gradient tightens. Gusts to around 30 mph are probable for channeled locations with 15 to 20 mph gusts expected elsewhere. Temperatures will sharply rise over today's highs in the low/mid 60s to the upper 60s to mid 70s by Wednesday afternoon. As the front and rainfall moves in Thursday, temperatures will begin to trend cooler with highs back in the 60s. KEY MESSAGE 2: Light radar returns are evident across the Canadian border with stronger returns evident in the vicinity of Lake Huron. These returns will track eastward through the day as a weak wave moves along the northern periphery of high pressure centered over the mid Atlantic states. Best chances for rain remain towards the Canadian border this afternoon and overnight with only a few hundredths to around 0.12" of rain. The next chances of rain will be on Thursday as the front moves into the region. Models are showing more of a consensus that the onset of precipitation will be earlier than previous forecasts beginning in the early morning hours across northern New York and by daybreak in Vermont. The biggest change has been in QPF which has sharply lowered as strongest forcing shifts south of the region. Chances are decreasing on amounts and most likely amounts falling below 0.25" Thursday. There are still a few ensemble members that have more forcing farther north, but those have been dwindling each run. KEY MESSAGE 3: At least a couple of chances for showers remains on track Friday through Monday; however, uncertainty in timing is large. As of now, the most likely scenario for precipitation forcing relates to a wave of low pressure developing to our southeast by Friday evening and working its way northeastward Saturday, while a trailing upper level low slowly crosses our region from the west. The potential for rainfall exceeding an inch has decreased with the latest ensemble guidance, as fewer members are supporting the idea of this low track retrograding to the northwest quickly enough to bring a conveyor belt of heavier rain this far north and west (as opposed to eastern New England). Instead, much of the rain over the weekend may be tied simply to showers that swing through in cyclonic, upslope flow. In general, the GEFS supports a faster progression of the upper level trough with weaker downstream blocking compared to the ENS, supporting a Friday night into Saturday timing as opposed to showers coming through later in the weekend into Monday. While there is plenty of uncertainty in the details, the shift to troughing will lead to a cooler and unsettled weather pattern into early next week even if there are extended dry periods for a given location. WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): BURLINGTON, Vt. (WCAX) -Happy Tuesday and election day! If you are heading out to the polls today, the weather is not looking too bad. I think most of the area has a good deal of cloud cover today, but it’s the further north that you are, where you have the better chance of seeing a few showers. To the south, while still cloudy, you stay mainly dry. Temperatures are kind of split in the upper 50s and lower 60s north with the chance of showers, but 60s to even a few lower 70s possible south where we stay dry. Tonight, lows fall back into the 50s as skies start to clear through the night. Wednesday will feel a lot more like September than early November as sunshine sends our temperatures soaring into the low and mid 70s. This will be warm enough to break or tie records all across the area. Again, all the warmth comes along with a good deal of sunshine. Clouds start to fill back in by Wednesday night, as lows fall back into the 50s. Thursday morning looks to start dry for most, before showers begin to roll through from west to east in the mid to late morning hours. Right now, it looks like we all see rain, but it’s not a ton with most only running a couple tenths of an inch of new rain. Temperatures are a tad cooler with most in the low to mid 60s. Friday looks drier, but there could still be a spotty shower here and there. We continue to lose a little bit of ground temperature wise, as most talk high temperatures in the upper 50s and lower 60s. The weekend could again feature a few showers for Saturday. Temperatures turn noticeably cooler with most only in the 40s to about 50 for Saturday afternoon. Sunday looks drier, but again could feature a spotty morning shower or two. Temperatures are generally stuck in the 40s for most.
NBC5 METEOROLOGIST (2026-11-02T23:29:00Z — same caveat): Mostly cloudy and cooler, few showers north Tuesday — Clouds thicken up tonight and it won't be too chilly, with lows in the 40s to around 50. Tuesday (Election Day) brings a mostly cloudy sky with passing light showers, mostly in northern areas, as a warm front lifts through. Highs will be near 60 there. Southern Vermont can expect more breaks of sun, with highs closer to 70. Wednesday looks to be the warmest day, as highs reach the low to mid-70s region-wide. Record highs are possible for many towns. Expect a mostly sunny sky. Thursday stays mild, with highs in the mid-60s. It turns breezy, with more clouds and a few showers arriving ahead of a cold front. Friday turns drier, though a few showers remain possible, especially south. Expect a mostly cloudy sky, as highs again reach the 60s. This weekend turns much cooler, an an upper-level low sends highs back closer to 50. Expect lots of clouds with additional showers possible, especially on Saturday.
